notes.title: Ver. 1.36.2 Minor corrections
notes.notes:
Linking errors in some city streets were corrected.

Forced the frame rate to be fixed to 60 fps.

The “Don't show distant wars” was changed to
changed to OFF by default.

notes.title: Ver. 1.36.1 Fix bug during CPU thinking
notes.notes:
On CPU turn,
In rare cases, the CPU would stop thinking and the game would stop,
Fixed a problem that caused the game to stop in rare cases.

Starting with this version, the game can be progressed even with saved data where the problem occurred and the game could not progress.
We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused to players.
We apologize for the inconvenience.

notes.title: Ver. 1.36.0 Correction of several bugs overlooked in the previous version
notes.notes:
Random events such as volunteer soldiers, etc. did not happen at all,
Fixed a bug in which only events related to the January disaster occurred.

Fixed a mistake when hiring a unit, where the unit's "EXP required for evolution" was not displayed correctly.

The parameters for farmland and mines are now blue text color when raised to the maximum value, though,
only worked when the territory's information window was on the left side, though,
Fixed so that it works on both.

Public investment, which should no longer be possible, is now possible,
A bug was reported in which public investments that should no longer be possible were being made, resulting in a decrease in money only, but no effect.

A bug has been reported that depending on the environment, the layout of the window before the start of the battle would be incorrect.
This has not been confirmed in the developer's environment, but we have confirmed that it can occur under certain conditions.
As a preventive measure, a slight delay has been added.

Changed the tax rate set by the CPU to be a little lower.

A bug has been reported that the Volunteer window disappears, but we have not been able to confirm this in the developer's environment.
As a precautionary measure, shortcut keys in windows with options such as Volunteers have been removed.
From this version,
It is no longer possible to cancel a volunteer event by right-clicking on it.

notes.title: Ver. 1.35.0 Display of experience required for evolution, correction of various
notes.notes:
How many experience values are required for a unit to be able to evolve,
The unit status will now display the number of experience required for units that can evolve.
Units that do not evolve will be marked as "No Evolution".

Previously, farmland and mine parameters were blue when they exceeded 200,
This is because these two parameters have different maximum values depending on the territory,
However, since the maximum values of these two parameters vary by territory, they did not make much sense as a guideline,
However, the blue text has been changed to indicate when the maximum value has been reached (when it cannot be increased any further).
The maximum value for walls is still 200 for all territories.

When the operation is left to the CPU in AUTO,
The button to cancel all AUTO operations is now always displayed in the upper left corner of the screen,
This makes it easier to cancel all AUTO operations.


Various bugs have been fixed.

There was a mistake in the calculation of unit maintenance fees,
The issue where maintenance fees were not being paid correctly has been corrected.

When a territory was rebelized, it was not handled correctly,
Fixed a bug that caused the icon and affiliation to be blank.

When a plot was launched against an insurgent territory,
The "civil war instigated" dialog would appear every time,
This has been prevented if the territory is already in a state of civil war.

Fixed a bug that prevented the public from investing when the investment should be less than 50, but it was only possible to invest when the investment was less than 50.

When the CPU selects a crop, the probability of selecting a crop with a high rate of return has been increased.
For example, a CPU whose territory is flat has a high probability of selecting "wheat" unless there is a disaster.

The event of changing agricultural disasters in January will now be shown as the highest priority.

MT-32 Phalanx" should only be found by search,
The problem of "MT-32 Phalanx" appearing as a volunteer soldier,
Preventive fixes have been made.

Some dialog boxes were turning red,
Preventive fixes have been made.

The Zorlond Peninsula and the Bourdon snowfield paths were out of order and have been fixed.

The term "Jibloa Mountains" has been changed to "Jibloa Forest.
The terrain in Isbrouck has been changed from mountainous to flat.

When you mouse over the red crown mark on the map, the following message appears,
The text "The boss is in this territory" has been changed to
The text "There is a strong enemy in this territory" has been changed to "There is a strong enemy in this territory".

notes.title: Ver. 1.34.0 Correction and prevention of some bugs
notes.notes:
Although there are cases where a definite or random event may occur at the beginning of a turn,
when they occur in multiple overlaps,
dialog when multiple events occur at the beginning of a turn,
This problem has been corrected so that one definite event has priority and random events do not occur in succession.

A small initialization process has been added to unit data during battle scenes.
This is intended to prevent bugs caused by unnecessary data.

Under certain conditions, a bug has been identified that prevents the dialog for volunteer soldiers from appearing.
As a remedy in case of a bug,
A button with the same function as the dialog is displayed only when a bug occurs.

The button is located behind the volunteer dialog,
It can only be accessed when the volunteer dialog is not displayed due to a bug.
Therefore, it cannot be seen in normal play,
You do not need to be concerned about it.
You can hire volunteers by pressing the emergency "YES" button.

notes.title: Ver. 1.33.0 Update on zoom of units in battle Other
notes.notes:
Regarding the size of the display of units in battle,
The size of units in battle is now variable and automatically adjusted based on the screen resolution set in the options,
The size of units in battle is now variable and automatically adjusted based on the screen resolution set in the options.

From this version, in the battle scene,
The size of units displayed in battle scenes will be adjusted to match the screen resolution.

In addition, some screen resolutions that could not be set before can now be selected.

This is useful when displaying certain dialog windows,
Fade processing, which could cause problems when displaying certain dialog windows, has been removed.

Graphics are now erased when the "Back" button is pressed.

notes.title: Ver. 1.32.1 Minor corrections
notes.notes: Fixed a very small portion of code that may cause unstable behavior.

notes.title: Ver. 1.32.0 The territory where the boss is located becomes visible. Other
notes.notes:
When it is the turn of the CPU's territory, the symbol of the territory may have a "red crown" like mark.
It indicates the territory where the boss is located.

The player should target this territory or avoid careless battles,
or to avoid careless battles.
The map does not indicate which boss is in the territory.
Also, the red crown symbol is not visible until the CPU starts a turn.

[Bug Fixes]

Fixed a bug that caused neutral territories to rebel.


[Change regarding weak units]

Against "weak units" set in a unit,
damage will be halved and attacks will be more likely to be dodged.
You will now struggle more explicitly against units you are not good at.

notes.title: Ver1.31.0 Number of territories reduced from 108 to 64, other bugs fixed.
notes.notes:
The number of territories has been reduced from 108 to 64, and the density between territories has been increased.

This medium-scale change was made to speed up the game play, which tended to become redundant.

Players now have fewer territories to conquer before clearing them,
The CPU's thinking time is reduced.

The world has changed from the previous version (Ver. 1.30.0 or later), so it is not possible to load saved data from the old version and play the game from this Ver. 1.31.0.

We apologize to players who have played through the previous version of the game.

Please enjoy the newly constructed world in the new game.

Other bugs that the button to speed up CPU's thinking was not displayed have been fixed.

notes.title: Fixed a bug that caused the UI to collapse in some screen resolutions.
notes.notes:
When playing a game with a resolution other than 1920x1080 set in the options,
Fixed a bug that caused some buttons to overlap and other UI displays to be incorrect.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused.

notes.title: Manual Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
The buttons in the manual table of contents and the scroll bar were not working.
They are working properly after the fix.
We apologize for the inconvenience.

notes.title: Ver. 1.29.0 Limit the number of public investments
notes.notes: Public investment can now be executed only once per turn.

notes.title: Ver. 1.28.0 Implementation of minimum remittance unit switching
notes.notes:
The unit of one unit that can be transferred with the "Remittance" command can be selected between "100G" and "1000G".

When using the "Remittance" command, a yellow button with the minimum unit of remittance will appear, and clicking it will switch the unit.

If the territory has more than 3000G in funds, the unit will be 1000G from the beginning,
If less than that, it will automatically be set to 100G.

notes.title: Ver. 1.27.0 Units without search capability will not be able to search.
notes.notes:
Units with too low search ability in the search command will no longer be able to search.

In addition, units with high INT but low exploration ability will be categorized as manual labor type and will be selected in automatic selection such as cultivation.

notes.title: Ver. 1.26.0 Improvement of public investment UI, etc.
notes.notes:
Previously, the public investment command was unfriendly as it did not show the effect of the investment, but we have made it a little more friendly by displaying the results.

Some public investments will now display changes in values after the investment.

In addition, to prevent wasteful investments, investments will no longer be allowed if they are not expected to have any effect at all.


Bug Fixes

In rare cases, the dialog window becomes transparent,
Fixed a bug that caused the dialog window to become transparent in rare cases and could not be fixed without restarting the game.

notes.title: Ver. 1.25.0 Addition of command to auto operate for one turn, etc.
notes.notes:
We implemented "Leave this turn to your subordinates.
When this command is used, the CPU will operate the territory for that turn only, and the next turn will switch to the player's operation.

It can be used to "pass" territories that are not often used.

The shortcut key is set to "A".

Changes to the strength of enemy units

Until now, enemy units have not been organized with extremely powerful units even in the final stages of the game,
The more the game heads toward the end of the game, the more extremely powerful the enemy's formation may become.

notes.title: Ver. 1.24.0 Fixed the bug that the ending does not transition.
notes.notes:
A bug that prevented the transition to the ending after conquering all territories has been corrected.

After the bug has been fixed, the ending will occur by "ending the turn" after conquering all territories.

We deeply apologize for any disappointment caused to players who had played the game until all territories were conquered.

notes.title: Ver. 1.23.0 Two exclusive BGMs for mid-bosses are added.
notes.notes:
Two new BGM songs were added and implemented as mid-boss songs.

One of the previously used mid-boss songs was discontinued.

notes.title: Ver. 1.22.0 Implementation of rebellion, changes in boss specifications
notes.notes:
In rare cases, a player's territory will rebel and his troops will betray him.
The rebellious troops become "insurgents" and turn against the player.

There are several conditions under which treachery can occur, all of which are related to the loyalty of the troops in the territory and their leader (lord).

The "Plot" command can also be used in rare instances to start a rebellion in the territory of an enemy who has plotted against you.

If a player uses the "Plot" command to turn a CPU territory into an insurgency, the CPUs become enemies with each other, but not with the player.


Changes to Boss Specifications

Until now, when the CPU territory was the last one, the boss would appear only when the difficulty was set to the highest level,
However, the boss will now appear on medium and hard difficulty levels.

notes.title: Ver. 1.21.0 Addition of dialog window direction
notes.notes: When some dialog windows are displayed, they are now staged to spread out from the center.

notes.title: Ver. 1.20.0 The current overall well-being of the territory is visualized to som
notes.notes:
The color of the map control tab changes according to the well-being of the entire territory of the player.

If the happiness of the territory's citizens is high, it is blue
Red if the well-being of the territory's citizens is low
Yellow for in-between
for the middle case.

instead of the happiness level of the currently operating territory unit,
The total happiness of all the territories will be used to determine the level of happiness of the territory.

notes.title: Ver. 1.19.0 Transition production was implemented.
notes.notes:
When changing scenes from the title screen to the loading screen or from the map screen to the battle screen,
When changing scenes from the title screen to the load screen, or from the map screen to the battle screen,
transition is performed when changing scenes from the title screen to the load screen, or from the map screen to the battle screen.

notes.title: Ver. 1.18.2 Bug correction of choice dialog
notes.notes:
Fixed a bug in the "Yes" and "No" choice dialog that caused "No" to be selected even if "Yes" was selected.

We apologize for the inconvenience.

notes.title: Ver. 1.18.0 Enhanced button presentation
notes.notes: When the mouse cursor is moused over a game button, the button is now enlarged and staged.

notes.title: Ver. 1.17.0 Nether Demon and Collector of Souls were added and implemented.
notes.notes:
Two units will be added.

Nether Demon

These are subterranean daemons that cannot be found by searching, etc., and will only offer to join as volunteer soldiers when the entire country is in ruins.
They appear in both player and CPU camps.
They are powerful units, but are so foul and evil that the mere presence of these units in a unit will cause the well-being of the territory to decline.


Collector of Souls

Demons of souls. A mid-boss character that appears after some progress in the game; only one appears during the game, and it is always hostile.

It is an extremely powerful daemon, ineffective against cold air, has no particular weakness, and can follow other advanced daemons.

notes.title: Ver. 1.16.3 Fix bug of Cusinart's proliferation
notes.notes:
We received a bug report that Cusinart was multiplying, so we fixed the bug.

We do not reproduce the bug as we consider it to be highly urgent, and the correction is based on our prediction of the location of the bug.

Fixed a code that may have caused multiple Cusinarts to appear.

After loading the game, if the game data already has more than one Cusinart,
Once all the Cusinarts are deleted, revert to a determination that no Cusinarts have appeared yet,
Cusinart is now repositioned.

We apologize to any players who were inconvenienced by this bug.

notes.title: Ver. 1.16.2 Minor corrections
notes.notes: Minor corrections were made for consistency with the trial version.

notes.title: Ver. 1.16.1 Some additions and corrections
notes.notes:
The "View:" and "Reroll Data" buttons in the new game are now supported by shortcuts to the "View:" and "Reroll Data" buttons, respectively.

Added a few more advice under distribution.

Fixed a bug in the display of the data window of the territory.

Adjusted the balance of disaster rates for each difficulty level.

notes.title: Ver. 1.16.0 Hireable units made visible at first country selection, etc.
notes.notes:
Until now, when selecting a country to operate in a new game, you did not know what units could be hired in that territory until you operated that territory,
We have made it possible to know this before deciding on the choice.

When you first select a country, there will be an orange button at the bottom of the screen that says "View :".

This button switches the window displaying the data of the territory between "Country Strength" and "Units".

When you select "National Strength," the data will continue to be displayed as before, including the numerical values of national strength,
Units" displays the types of units that can be hired.

Clicking the "Reroll Data" button will shuffle the country power and available units.
If your country's strength is weak or you don't like it, you can shuffle the data.
(The more rural the country, the weaker the national strength.)


Fixed a problem where there were too few disasters than expected.

The price of advanced units (special units) that can be hired from the beginning has been lowered.

notes.title: Ver. 1.15.1 Improvement of display renponses
notes.notes: The display of unit statuses when the cursor is moved over a unit in commands such as "Search" and "Decide on a lord" has been improved, as it was difficult to display the statuses of the unit, resulting in poor response.

notes.title: Ver. 1.15.0 Unit: "Mystic Jester" and "Mad Crown" additionally implemented
notes.notes:
Two new units were added and implemented.

Mad Crown

A crazy clown. He has low offensive ability but strong luck, and is dexterous, quick, and very good at evading close attacks.
He will only join you by the way you explore and find him in your territory.

Mystic Jester

Mystic Clown. He is dexterous, quick and very good at evading close attacks.
It has a stubbornness that is not possible for ordinary creatures, and attacks by shooting flames from its mouth as if it were an acrobatic act.
It is a mid-boss unit that appears after a certain amount of time in the game, and only one of them appears in the game, and it always opposes the player.

notes.title: Ver. 1.14.1 Some minor changes
notes.notes: Several changes were made to the game balance, such as not allowing marine units to be found in search in marshy areas.

notes.title: Ver. 1.14.0 Unit: Addition of Knight Errant and Cusinart
notes.notes:
The "Knight Errant" unit has been implemented.

They are itinerant knights who make their living as adventurers and mercenaries, and can only be found in searches or appear as volunteer soldiers.
They are experts in close combat with a good balance of physical strength, attack power, and hit rate, but they do not have long-range attacks.
They are vulnerable to energy attacks and have a high cost.

The "Cusinart" unit has been implemented.

He is an itinerant knight who calls himself "Cusinart" a hero from a previous war 130 years ago.
He is a mid-boss unit that appears when the game progresses to a certain degree, and there is only one of him in the game, and he will always oppose the player.

notes.title: Ver. 1.13.0 Implementation of Unit: Raven
notes.notes:
Raven was added to the units.

It is a huge crow that specializes in the snowfields. Its beak and claws are not so strong, but it can dexterously throw huge rocks from the sky and attack at long range.
Its flight makes it difficult to hit with close attacks, but wind magic is its weakness.

notes.title: Ver. 1.12.0 Unit : Hornbeetle is added and implemented.
notes.notes:
Hornbeetle was additionally implemented.

It is an omnivorous, huge beetle with sharp horns and lives in forested areas.
It sometimes hunts animals and other animals by lunging at its prey with its horns, and it also sips dead flesh.

They are good at fighting because of their strong arms and physical strength, but their low intelligence prevents them from working in domestic affairs, and they are weak in cold places and cold air is their weakness.

notes.title: ver.1.11.2 Minor bug fixes
notes.notes:
Fixed a problem in which the shortcut key for both "Move Unit" and "Develop Mine" was set to "M".
The "I" key is now assigned for "Move Units.

Fixed a mistake in which closing the window by pressing the Esc key or other keys after executing a public investment on the public investment screen would terminate the public investment.
Only the window will be closed.

notes.title: Ver. 1.11.1 Fixed a progression loss bug.
notes.notes:
Fixed a fatal bug that caused the player to lose progress after defeating a mid-boss unit.

Fixed a bug that shortcut V did not work.

notes.title: Ver. 1.11.0 Display of number of units in battle
notes.notes:
In battle scenes, a symbol indicating the number of units is displayed at the bottom of the screen so that the number of attacking and defending units participating in the battle can be determined at a glance.

Red dolls represent the number of attackers and blue dolls represent the number of defenders.
If the walls are functioning, the wall icon is also displayed.

notes.title: Ver. 1.10.0 Added the ability to forecast earnings for the next turn when the ta
notes.notes:
On the Change Tax Rate screen, in the earnings report that appears in the lower left corner when the tax rate is changed,
(+) column now shows the projected increase or decrease in tax revenues when the tax rate is changed.
When tax revenue is changed,

Crop: +300 (+30G)

then the tax revenue of the crop for the next turn is expected to be +330G.
The value is not a fixed value, so it may not be as expected due to disasters and other reasons.


When moving a territory, if no units were in the territory, the move command could not be used and units could not be called in from a friendly territory.
The move command can now be used even when there is no unit in the territory.
However, the move command cannot be used when there are no units and the player has only one territory.

notes.title: Ver. 1.9.0 Shortcut key support for most commands, etc.
notes.notes:
Some commands, such as "cultivate farmland" and "search," can now be called up with shortcut keys.
The supported keys are written in the message window that appears when the cursor is placed over the command icon.
If it says "Hire Unit [h]," then the H key is the key to call the Hire Unit command.

The list of territories that appears when you click on a territory is not a list of territories in order of operation,
The list has been changed to show the number and name of all the territories connected to that territory by road.

Some windows that were not displayed since the last update have been fixed to be displayed.

notes.title: Ver. 1.8.2 Some changes and updates
notes.notes:
Until now, the only way to see the detailed status of a unit was through the "View Troops" or "Employment" commands,
It is now also displayed in the Pioneering, Developing, Building, Moving, Dismissing, Plotting, Appointing Lords, Scouting, and Dungeon Defeating commands.
Comments about the graphics and characteristics of your army units can only be seen in the "View Troops" command.

The map screen can now be scrolled by holding down the right mouse button (or left Ctrl) and dragging the map with the left mouse button.

Previously, units that could be hired with the "Hire Units" command could be bought with borrowed money, even if you had zero money, and you could fill up your troops even if you had no money.
However, if you borrowed money, your funds would go negative and you would not be able to move units until they were paid back, and their loyalty would decrease due to non-payment, and eventually they would quit.
Units found by volunteer troops and exploration were forced to cancel their membership if they did not have enough funds, so only hiring commands could borrow money.
However, this makes the rules ambiguous and it is misleading to allow players to go into debt unintentionally, so we have made it basically impossible to go into debt in hiring units.

It is still possible to default on a debt by incurring the cost of maintaining a unit, or by paying a settlement with the revolting lords.

The information about a territory can now be viewed by hovering the cursor over the territory window, but when the cursor is released, the window will switch to the territory being operated on.

notes.title: Ver. 1.8.1 Display of culture and industry additive values
notes.notes:
In the territory information window, the culture and industry data now displays the value added in the previous turn.

Culture is added or subtracted by the lord's ability in the form of a (+).

Industries are added or subtracted by the well-being of the population in the form of a (+).

This does not include figures that change due to public works, disasters, wars, etc., but purely due to domestic politics.

It is not a simple matter of the lord being good and the lord being incompetent, but the increase or decrease may be a factor in determining whether a lord is the right person for the job.

notes.title: Ver. 1.8.0 The order of territories to be operated can now be confirmed.
notes.notes:
In the previous version, the order of the territories to be operated was unclear,
This version shows the order.
In the data of the territories, a number is displayed next to the name of the territory.
The order of the turnover is from 1 to the next.

Also, if you click on the symbol of a territory with no commands, you will see a list of the order of the territories up to 16 places ahead.
Territories in blue in the list are the player's territories,
Red territories are enemy territories that may invade the player's territory.

Clicking on a territory name in the list will move the map to that territory's location and switch the list to start from there.

You may get some idea of the next possible invasion when you finish a turn.

notes.title: Ver. 1.7.2 Improvement of key response and correction of other bugs
notes.notes:
The key used for "Decide" can now optionally be selected as the Space key in addition to the Enter key.

Improved keyboard response.
When two or more "Close" buttons appear on the employment screen, etc., pressing the Esc key presses both buttons at the same time.
The Esc key can now also be used to close the unit's graphic window, which can be seen in the unit list, etc.

In the unit's movement between allied territories, a mistake has been corrected in which the 10th unit did not have its strength determined by the color of the text.

Other minor fixes have been made.

notes.title: Ver. 1.7.1 Three small updates
notes.notes:
Previously, when no commands were used, the territory information window was fixed to the operating territory and the information of other territories could not be seen,
From this version, information is displayed when you hover the cursor over the symbol of another territory.
To make it easier to distinguish between the operating territory and the other territories, the color of the window is different for the two.

"Esc" key cancels or closes the window.
"Enter" to make a decision.

A new option "Do not confirm in the dialog box at the end of the turn" has been added.
By turning it on, the turn of the territory will end immediately without confirmation when the end-of-turn command button is pressed.
This option is off by default.

notes.title: Ver. 1.7.0 When a unit is full, it is now possible to dismiss and replace unwant
notes.notes:
Until now, when a unit was full, a new unit could not join unless a vacancy was created in advance,
However, from this version, when a new unit joins and the unit is full, the "Dismiss Unit" command can be used on the spot to dismiss and replace unwanted members.

From now on, it should no longer be necessary to keep a unit at nine members at all times for the sake of units and volunteers that you find in your search.

A few other minor bugs have been fixed.

notes.title: Ver. 1.6.0 Advanced units can now be hired. Other changes related to difficulty
notes.notes:
In the "Hire Units" command, only one type of higher level unit can be hired for each territory, which is stronger than the normal hired units.
Higher level units are indicated by a blue button.
The price is very much more expensive than the price for joining a unit through exploration or volunteer soldiers.

The strength of units in the earliest enemy territories on medium difficulty is slightly weakened.
The CPU does not explore in the earliest stages of the game as it does in difficulty casual.

Eliminated the "clear on medium difficulty" requirement for unlocking modes in which backstage bosses appear.
The highest difficulty level can be unlocked even if the game is cleared on casual difficulty.
The achievements are now the same for both Casual and Medium difficulty levels, making it easier for players to choose the difficulty level that best suits their needs.

notes.title: Ver. 1.5.0 Revamped movement of units between allied territories, other correcti
notes.notes:
In the previous version, friendly territories could only go from the source to the destination and could not move if the destination was full,
However, from this version, it is now possible to switch units between the source and the destination.
Units can be called in from a specified friendly territory, or units can be switched even if both territories are full.
Movements are not confirmed until the "Perform Move" button is pressed, and the "Back" button must be pressed to cancel.

Fixed a fatal bug that caused the CPU to freeze when using the "Public Works" command.

Changed the conditions for the appearance of bosses.
Bosses will no longer appear early in the game.
Saved data that has already appeared will not be affected.

notes.title: Ver. 1.4.1 Correction of button display during withdrawal and other minor correc
notes.notes:
Fixed a bug in which the "Decide Member" button was incorrectly displayed when a unit had already died and disappeared from the list when withdrawal was selected during a battle.

Other minor fixes.

notes.title: Ver1.4.0 Addition of "Do not show distant wars" option
notes.notes:
Added an option to hide CPU wars that occur outside of neighboring countries.
This option is enabled by checking the "Do not show distant wars" checkbox in the option settings.

All information about which territories, what kind of organization, war results, etc., will no longer be displayed.
Wars in CPU territories adjacent to the player's territory will be displayed.

This setting is set to ON by default.

notes.title: Ver. 1.3.2 Relaxation of conditions for recovery of physical strength
notes.notes:
Until now, in order to recover the health of a damaged unit, it was necessary to rest without performing any action,
This condition has been eliminated, and units will regain strength regardless of whether or not they have taken any action.

When "automatic selection" is used to cultivate farmland, etc., the unit with reduced health will be selected.

notes.title: Ver. 1.3.1 Display of unit levels, etc.
notes.notes:
The "level" of a unit, which has existed internally, will now be displayed as "(unit name)-L(level)" on the status and battle screens.

Levels range from 1 to 7, and are raised incrementally by accumulating experience.

As the level increases, the unit acquires a very powerful correction that reduces the damage of any attack.

For example, a level 2 unit will avoid and nullify 100% of all 1 damage, no matter what the attack is.

It takes 10000 experience to raise a unit to the maximum level of 7.

A bug has been fixed in which using retreat in battle would end the action of a unit that did not go to the battlefield and was waiting in its own territory, even if it was ready to act.

notes.title: Ver. 1.3.0 Enabled to see information on enemy units in battle. Other balance ad
notes.notes:
When a player is attacking an enemy territory, the "View Troop" button can now also show information on the enemy's troops.

Pressing the "Friendly Units" button will switch to the "Enemy Units" button, which will display a list of enemy units.

The find rate of higher class units found by the "Search" command has been increased by 5% to make them easier to find.

notes.title: Ver. 1.2.0 Withdrawal from battle as a single unit was implemented.
notes.notes:
Previously, only whole units could withdraw from battle, but from this version, units can do so individually, so it is no longer necessary for all allies to withdraw in order to preserve a single allied unit that is about to die with lots of experience.

When you select "Withdrawal" in battle, a checklist of units will be lined up, and you must uncheck the units you wish to disengage.
When the "Decide Member" button appears, press it and only the unchecked units will withdraw from the battlefield and return to their home countries.
If you wish to withdraw all units together, click the "Withdraw All" button.

notes.title: Ver. 1.1.1 The incidence of disasters changes with difficulty level. Other
notes.notes:
The rate of disaster occurrence was constant at all levels of game difficulty, but starting from this version, the rate of disaster occurrence has been changed to

[b]Casual - 50% reduction in the incidence of disasters
Medium - 30% less disasters
Hard - same rate as before[/b]

The rate of disasters becomes milder with each difficulty level,
If the difficulty level is below medium, the "mild climate" will be more frequent.

However, only floods and revolts are not affected by the difficulty level.

Currently, a bug has been reported in CPU battles where the battle loops with all the players being wiped out from the beginning.
It is difficult to reproduce the bug, so for now, we have applied a process to abort the war if the CPU does not select any units to send to the battlefield when it makes a decision to go to war.

notes.title: Ver. 1.1.0 Display of lines connecting territories, etc.
notes.notes:
When the mouse cursor is hovered over a territory symbol, a yellow line is now displayed to make it easier to identify other territories that can be moved from the symbol.

The problem where the "Back" button in the unit list would disappear when right-clicking to close the window after displaying a unit's graphic in the unit list, making progress impossible, has been addressed.
The "Close" button on a window displaying a unit's graphic no longer works when right-clicking.

notes.title: Ver. 1.0.3 Cancel by right click, etc.
notes.notes:
It is now possible to "cancel" or "close" most windows by right-clicking the mouse.

Game pause is moved to the Pause key on the keyboard.

The acquired earnings for that turn are now displayed in parentheses () next to "Funds".

notes.title: Ver. 1.0.2 Display of work efficiency, etc.
notes.notes:
In commands in which a unit performs a task, such as "cultivate farmland," the power value of the unit's work efficiency is now displayed when the cursor is hovered over the unit name on the unit list.
This will allow you to see if the unit will succeed at the task efficiently.

Fixed a bug that caused enemy units to be seen unconditionally when using the Recon command to reconnoiter a friendly territory and then reconnoiter an enemy territory.

Removed unnecessary keyboard operations on the map screen.

notes.title: Version that fixed a critical bug.
notes.notes:
Fixed a bug that caused the "End Battle" button to not appear when all allied troops were wiped out in enemy territory, making progress impossible.

Our apologies.
